channel.title: AIScroll - AI News & Insights
channel.description: Latest AI news, trends, and insights. Stay updated with the AI industry.

item.title: Muse Spark 1.3 Tops OpenCode Daily Usage
item.description: Muse Spark 1.3 topped OpenCode daily token usage two days after launch, converting Meta's Contributor strategy and massive AI spending into live adoption.

item.title: September AI Race: Five Labs Enter the Field
item.description: Claude Fable 5.1 set a new benchmark as Gemini and Muse closed in. With GPT Astra and Grok 4.7 on deck, September has become a five-lab frontier race.

item.title: Chinese AI Models Reach the Frontier
item.description: GLM-5.3-Flash, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, and Kimi K3 scored 56–57 on AAII, landing within 4–7 points of leading US frontier models.

item.title: Gemini 3.5 Pro Shelved for Gemini 4?
item.description: Gemini 3.5 Pro missed its June launch as Google began Gemini 4 pretraining. Reliance on 3.7 Flash and key researcher departures compound the delay.

item.title: Why Frontier AI Releases Stalled
item.description: Anthropic kept Model 2 internal while OpenAI paused Astra training. Chinese models are closing the gap at far lower prices.

item.title: xAI After Cursor: Grok 4.6 and Grok Bot Surge
item.description: SpaceXAI pairs its Cursor acquisition with Grok 4.6 and Grok Bot, turning model gains, developer distribution, and subscription bundling into a frontier push.

item.title: Grok 4.6 Launch Set: xAI Targets the Frontier
item.description: Musk announced Grok 4.6 for August 7. Following Grok 4.5's successful month, xAI aims to challenge the frontier held by Opus 5, Fable 5, and GPT-5.6.

item.title: OpenAI Cuts GPT-5.6 Prices; DeepSeek Fires Back
item.description: OpenAI cut GPT-5.6 Luna prices by 80% on July 30. A day later, DeepSeek released a V4 Flash update, squeezing premium-priced Anthropic from both ends.

item.title: Claude Opus 5 Early Reviews: Efficiency King
item.description: Claude Opus 5 leads intelligence index post-launch. Users praise its token efficiency, though Fable 5 remains ahead in general-purpose capabilities.

item.title: GPT-5.6 Wins Early Praise on Price and Power
item.description: GPT-5.6 earns early praise for performance and value. As OpenAI expanded usage perks, Anthropic extended its limits and model-access offers in response.

item.title: GPT-5.6 Leaves Claude Without Its Edge
item.description: GPT-5.6 has caught up while ChatGPT offers the stronger bundle. With Fable 5 gone from plans, Claude has lost its clearest user-facing edge.

item.title: Mythos: Sovereign AI Scale Race, Memory Crunch
item.description: Mythos made frontier AI a national-security asset. Larger-scale pretraining and sovereign AI data-center expansion are expected to lift HBM and DRAM demand.

item.title: GPT-5.6 Price War Hits Anthropic at Its Weakest
item.description: Sonnet 5 backlash and Fable 5 leaving subscriptions collide with OpenAI's half-price GPT-5.6 family. Terra matches GPT-5.5 at half the cost.

item.title: Anthropic's Release Sprint: A Sign of Self-Improvement?
item.description: With Fable 5 and Mythos 5 out, Anthropic's rapid releases outpace rivals, sparking speculation on X about recursive self-improvement.

item.title: Sakana Fugu: Sovereign AI or Borrowed SOTA?
item.description: Sakana AI pitches Fugu as 'sovereign AI.' Critics argue its Fable 5-level benchmark measures borrowed closed-model performance, not Fugu's own capability.

item.title: Trump: Amazon Triggered Fable Halt
item.description: Trump identified the competitor and co-shareholder that reported Anthropic. Why did Amazon, its $8B lead investor, turn in its own bet to Washington?

item.title: Sovereign AI and the Mythos Kill Switch
item.description: Washington's block on Anthropic's Fable 5 triggered a European 'kill switch' panic. The same day, China's open GLM-5.2 challenged US AI dominance.

item.title: The Agent Mix: One Orchestrator, Many Models
item.description: The era of the single AI model is fading. Costly frontier models now orchestrate cheaper task-specific ones, uniting Grok, Gemini, GPT, and DeepSeek.

item.title: Warsh's Fed Casts AI as 'American Ingenuity'
item.description: At his first FOMC meeting, new Fed Chair Kevin Warsh framed AI as 'American ingenuity,' betting productivity gains can tame inflation.

item.title: Amodei's Iran School Strike Remark Backlash
item.description: Amodei called the Iran school strike that killed 120 children a case that 'doesn't violate our red lines' — even as Claude powers the Maven targeting system.

item.title: Apple Signals Price Hikes as Memory Costs Soar
item.description: Apple CEO Tim Cook has warned that price hikes are unavoidable across its product lineup as AI data center demand drains memory supplies.

item.title: Noam Shazeer Leaves Google for OpenAI
item.description: Noam Shazeer, Transformer co-author and Gemini co-lead, is leaving Google for OpenAI — a star it paid $2.7B to bring back, stirring fears of internal turmoil.

item.title: GLM-5.2 Overtakes Gemini 3.5 Flash
item.description: Four days after launch, GLM-5.2 hit 51 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, edging out Gemini 3.5 Flash — the top open-weight score yet.

item.title: Microsoft Eyes DeepSeek to Cut Copilot Costs
item.description: Microsoft is weighing self-hosted DeepSeek for Copilot to cut costs, as GLM-5.2, Kimi K2.7 and DeepSeek V4 near frontier quality far more cheaply.

item.title: Cursor Teases From-Scratch Frontier Model
item.description: Cursor teased a new frontier model at Compile — trained from scratch, no Kimi base, with 10–20x Composer's compute. It ships within weeks.

item.title: SpaceX to Acquire Cursor in $60 Billion Deal
item.description: SpaceX will buy Anysphere, maker of AI coding tool Cursor, for $60 billion in stock — four days after its record IPO, a bet on its lagging AI unit.

item.title: Anthropic Pauses Claude Agent SDK Credit Plan
item.description: Anthropic abruptly shelved its June 15 Agent SDK credit system on launch day, days after the forced Fable 5 shutdown rattled subscriber trust.

item.title: Top 5 Coding Agents of H1 2026, Ranked
item.description: A ranking of the top five coding agents of H1 2026: Claude Code leads on quality despite a cost backlash, with Codex closing in fast.

item.title: Samsung Foundry Wins Neuralink 4nm Chip Order
item.description: Samsung Foundry has won its first Neuralink order to make the fourth-gen brain-implant chip on a 4nm process. First test silicon ships in H1 2027.

item.title: xAI Trade Secret Suit Tossed; Musk Loses Again
item.description: A California court permanently dismissed xAI's trade secret suit against OpenAI, finding no proof that OpenAI itself directed the theft of Grok's code.

item.title: Le Chaton Fat: Mistral's Fake AI Model Hoax
item.description: In June 2026, a fake Mistral AI model called 'Le Chaton Fat' went viral on X with fabricated benchmarks and parody press releases — even drawing in the CEO.

item.title: Anthropic, White House Negotiate Fable 5 Return
item.description: Anthropic has entered talks with the White House to undo the suspension of Fable 5 and Mythos 5. It expects a fast return, but both stayed offline on June 15.

item.title: GLM-5.2: Great Model, Shaky Coding Plan
item.description: Three days after release, developer sentiment on GLM-5.2 is split: the model's coding draws praise, but users blast the Z.ai Coding Plan's quotas.

item.title: OpenRouter Unveils Fusion, a Compound AI Model
item.description: OpenRouter launched Fusion, a multi-model mode that runs several AI models in parallel and fuses them into one answer at roughly half the frontier cost.

item.title: 42 State Attorneys General Probe OpenAI
item.description: A coalition of 42 U.S. attorneys general opened a probe into OpenAI, subpoenaing records on ads, data and minors—days after its confidential IPO filing.

item.title: Cartoonish: AI World Reacts to Fable Shutdown
item.description: A US order barring foreign access pulled Fable 5 and Mythos 5 three days after launch. Reactions on X ran from 'cartoonish' to 'reaps what one sows.'

item.title: Did Amazon Help Trigger Anthropic's Model Ban?
item.description: The Information says Amazon's Andy Jassy raised security concerns over Anthropic's models to the Trump administration, helping prompt Fable and Mythos curbs.

item.title: GLM-5.2 Open Source as US Blocks Fable 5
item.description: The day Washington barred foreign nationals from Anthropic's Fable 5 and Mythos 5, China's Z.ai launched GLM-5.2, with open MIT weights due next week.

item.title: Claude Fable 5 Suspended on US Export Order
item.description: The US government ordered Anthropic to bar foreign access to Fable 5 and Mythos 5. Unable to block selectively, it disabled both models for all users.

item.title: SpaceX IPO: $75B Raise, SPCX Soars in Debut
item.description: SpaceX completed the largest IPO in history, raising $75 billion at $135 a share. SPCX opened at $150 on Nasdaq and hit an intraday high of $176.52.

item.title: GPT-5.5 Pro Spotted in Codex App Settings
item.description: An unannounced GPT-5.5 Pro entry surfaced in Codex app settings on June 11, hinting OpenAI is about to bring its top reasoning model to the coding agent.

item.title: Gemini 3.5 Pro Leak: Is Google Falling Behind?
item.description: A leaked checkpoint analysis suggests Gemini 3.5 Pro trails competitors in reasoning and coding, though the unreleased model's performance remains unverified.

item.title: Kimi K2.7 Code: Moonshot Cuts Reasoning 30%
item.description: Moonshot AI open-sourced Kimi K2.7 Code, cutting reasoning tokens 30% vs K2.6 while raising coding scores. Weights and API shipped the same day.

item.title: Windows Local AI Opens Up to Nvidia RTX GPUs
item.description: Microsoft now lets Windows 11's local Language Model APIs run on Nvidia RTX 30+ GPUs with 6GB VRAM, eroding the Copilot+ PC's NPU-only exclusivity.

item.title: Codex Adds Referral Resets After 5M Milestone
item.description: OpenAI adds a referral program to Codex: invite a friend, earn a rate-limit reset. The perk lands as Codex tops 5 million weekly active users.

item.title: Claude Tops Korea's Paid Generative AI Market
item.description: Claude passed ChatGPT in Korea's paid AI market with 49.5 billion won in March card payments. Sensor Tower shows it passing Gemini with top revenue growth.

item.title: CISA Orders 3-Day Patching for Riskiest Flaws
item.description: CISA's BOD 26-04 cuts the patch window for the riskiest flaws to 3 days as AI accelerates exploitation, while letting agencies defer low-risk bugs.

item.title: Meta Severs Manus Ties After China Unwind Order
item.description: Meta cut off data sharing with Manus, completing an operational split after China ordered the $2B deal unwound. Founders seek $1B to buy the company back.

item.title: Anthropic Moves to Ease Fable 5 Over-Refusals
item.description: Anthropic has pledged to cut Claude Fable 5's false positives after users reported harmless scientific prompts being routed to the older Opus 4.8.

item.title: OpenAI Weighs Drastic Token Price Cuts
item.description: OpenAI is weighing deep token price cuts to preempt rival Anthropic, the WSJ reports, days after the startup confidentially filed for an IPO.

item.title: Claude Fable 5 Early Reviews: 'A Step Change'
item.description: A day after launch, Claude Fable 5 is drawing rave reviews. Stripe finished a 50M-line migration in one day; Karpathy calls it a generational step change.

item.title: Google Unveils Gemini 3.5 Live Translate
item.description: Google has launched Gemini 3.5 Live Translate, a dedicated audio model designed for real-time simultaneous interpretation across more than 70 languages.

item.title: OpenAI in Talks to Lease 10GW Ohio AI Campus
item.description: OpenAI is in advanced talks to lease a 10GW AI campus in Ohio for 20 years, with Nvidia weighing a credit guarantee on a buildout estimated at $500 billion.

item.title: Claude Fable 5: SOTA on Nearly Every Benchmark
item.description: Anthropic launched Claude Fable 5, its first public Mythos-class model. It tops SWE-bench Verified at 95% and sets SOTA on nearly every benchmark.

item.title: Claude Fable 5: Nerfed Mythos Sparks Backlash
item.description: Anthropic released Claude Fable 5, a Mythos-class model. Users are furious over sensitive queries routed to Opus 4.8 and plan access ending June 22.

item.title: Claude Mythos Nears Launch: Fable 5 Surfaces
item.description: The 'claude-fable-5' identifier spotted on Microsoft Azure suggests Anthropic is preparing a public, safeguarded build of its flagship Claude Mythos.

item.title: Siri Is Not Gemini: Apple’s 20B On-Device Model
item.description: Contrary to headlines that Gemini powers the new Siri, Apple's own docs reveal its on-device brain is a homegrown 20B model: AFM 3 Core Advanced.

item.title: OpenAI Confidentially Files for IPO
item.description: OpenAI confidentially filed a draft S-1 with the SEC on June 8, joining Anthropic and SpaceX in a $1 trillion IPO race at an $852 billion valuation.

item.title: Surface Laptop Ultra Takes On MacBook Pro
item.description: Microsoft unveiled the Surface Laptop Ultra, its most powerful yet, pairing NVIDIA's RTX Spark with 128GB of unified memory to challenge the MacBook Pro.

item.title: GitHub Copilot's Usage-Based Billing Backlash
item.description: GitHub Copilot's June 1 shift to token-based billing sparked backlash, with users projecting 50x costs and an exodus after a second pricing overhaul in a year.

item.title: Huawei Ascend 910C Post-Trains DeepSeek V4-Pro
item.description: A Huawei-led team post-trained DeepSeek's 1.6T V4-Pro on 1,000+ Ascend 910C chips—Chinese silicon reaching training, though no benchmarks were shared.

item.title: June 2026 Coding Agents: Opus 4.8 vs GPT-5.5
item.description: Claude Opus 4.8 leads June 2026's coding agents, with GPT-5.5 closing the gap on backend. Composer 2.5 and Gemini 3.5 Flash follow on value and frontend.

item.title: ‘Chat Is Dead’: AI Labs Pivot to Agents
item.description: OpenAI is rebuilding ChatGPT into an autonomous agent super app, and rivals Google, Anthropic, and Microsoft are shifting from chatbots to agents too.

item.title: Apple's Siri Rebuilt on Google Gemini at WWDC
item.description: Apple unveils a rebuilt Siri at WWDC 2026, powered by a custom 1.2-trillion-parameter Google Gemini model that costs Apple about $1 billion a year.

item.title: AI Has Solved Coding and Math Contests
item.description: OpenAI's Noam Brown says math and coding contests will soon lose their appeal after AI swept the 2025 IMO, IOI, and ICPC. Next: unsolved problems.

item.title: GPT-5.6 Checkpoints: A Real Vision Upgrade
item.description: Unreleased GPT-5.6 checkpoints show a marked jump in vision—long the GPT-5.x weak spot. Sharper SVG output has testers calling the model ahead of Gemini.

item.title: Google to Rent xAI Compute for $920M a Month
item.description: Google will pay SpaceX $920 million a month for about 110,000 Nvidia GPUs at xAI's Colossus data center, just ahead of SpaceX's record IPO.

item.title: Japan Warns It Could Become an 'AI Colony'
item.description: Digital Minister Hisashi Matsumoto says Japan risks becoming an 'AI colony,' defending a bill to let AI train on sensitive data without consent.

item.title: Meta Hatch: Vibe-Coding Agent Built on Claude
item.description: Meta is developing a consumer vibe-coding agent codenamed Hatch — built on Anthropic's Claude, bound for its own Muse Spark, with a $199.99 tier in play.

item.title: Claude Mythos Early Reviews Split Sharply
item.description: Early feedback on Anthropic's Claude Mythos splits sharply: some testers praise its automated security skills while others call the performance mediocre.

item.title: Anthropic Helps NSA Use Mythos for Cyberattacks
item.description: The NSA is deploying Anthropic's Mythos AI in offensive cyber operations, the FT reports — even as Anthropic sues the Pentagon, the NSA's parent agency.

item.title: Why Open Source Is Drawing the Line on AI Slop
item.description: Godot now bans fully AI-generated contributions, curl killed its bug bounty, and Jazzband shut down. How open source is drawing a line against AI slop.

item.title: Anthropic Warns AI Self-Improvement Is Near
item.description: Anthropic's internal data shows AI is accelerating its own development. Warning recursive self-improvement may be near, it urges a global pause mechanism.

item.title: DeepSeek Tops US Business Spending Tracker
item.description: DeepSeek topped Ramp's June first-purchase index for US firms. Adoption is just 0.1%, but direct payments route corporate data to China-hosted servers.

item.title: US Eyes AI Equity Stakes for Public Dividends
item.description: Trump officials held early talks about taking equity stakes in major AI firms, with returns distributed as dividends to American households.

item.title: Claude Mythos 2 Rumor: A Day on X
item.description: Claude Mythos 2 rumors swept X on June 3-4 after the AI Security Institute reported gains for a newer checkpoint — is a new model under test?

item.title: Microsoft's Project Solara: Agents, Not Apps
item.description: At Build 2026, Microsoft introduced Project Solara — a chip-to-cloud platform for devices that run AI agents instead of apps, built on Android, not Windows.

item.title: GPT, Grok, Claude Open Up; Gemini Holds Out
item.description: OpenAI, xAI, and Anthropic now let subscribers sign into third-party tools with their own accounts. Only Gemini bans it, suspending paying users who try.

item.title: Gemma 4 12B: An Encoder-Free Multimodal Model
item.description: Google's Gemma 4 12B runs locally on a 16GB laptop yet nears its 26B MoE, dropping multimodal encoders and shipping with Multi-Token Prediction by default.

item.title: ChatGPT App Tops 1 Billion Monthly Users
item.description: ChatGPT's mobile app crossed 1 billion monthly active users in May, per Sensor Tower — the fastest app ever to hit the mark, in about three years.

item.title: OpenAI Goes All-In on the App Layer With Python
item.description: OpenAI shipped a wave of Python SDK releases in early 2026—Agent sandboxes, a Codex SDK, Bedrock GA—an all-in bet on the AI application layer.

item.title: Trump's AI Order: Voluntary 30-Day Model Review
item.description: Trump signed an AI executive order on June 2 asking frontier model developers to voluntarily submit systems for government testing 30 days before release.

item.title: Microsoft Unveils Reasoning Model MAI-Thinking-1
item.description: Microsoft unveiled MAI-Thinking-1, its first in-house reasoning model, at Build 2026 — trained from scratch, no distillation, rivaling Claude Opus 4.6 on code.

item.title: Korean Giants Secure Anthropic's Mythos Access
item.description: Samsung, SK Hynix, and SK Telecom are the first Korean firms to join Anthropic's 'Project Glasswing,' gaining access to its 'AI hacker' model Mythos.

item.title: MiniMax M3: Open-Weight 1M-Context Coding Rival
item.description: MiniMax launched M3, a coding model with a 1M-token context via MSA, priced at a fraction of frontier rivals. Open-weight, but the training code stays closed.

item.title: GPT-5.5-Codex-Spark Appears on Pricing Page
item.description: OpenAI listed GPT-5.5-Codex-Spark (research preview) on its Codex pricing page with no official post—a sign the rollout is near.

item.title: Anthropic Doubles Claude Limits With Colossus
item.description: Anthropic secured all of SpaceX's Colossus 1 capacity and doubled Claude's usage limits, answering months of cost and rate-limit complaints.

item.title: Anthropic Opens Claude Mythos to the EU
item.description: Anthropic offered the EU's cybersecurity agency ENISA access to its top model Claude Mythos on June 1, the first EU body to get it, as a wider rollout nears.

item.title: Composer 2.5 Lands on Grok Build: xAI-Cursor Tie
item.description: xAI added Cursor's Composer 2.5 to Grok Build on June 1 — an external model that out-codes its own. The first product signal of the SpaceX-xAI-Cursor stack.

item.title: Anthropic Files Confidentially for IPO
item.description: Anthropic submitted a confidential draft registration statement to the SEC on June 1, positioning itself alongside SpaceX and OpenAI in a historic race for a trillion-dollar public debut.

item.title: NVIDIA Vera Rubin Enters Full Production
item.description: NVIDIA has announced full production of its next-generation Vera Rubin AI platform at GTC 2026. Equipped with 288GB of HBM4 and delivering 50 petaflops of FP4 inference per GPU, the platform directly targets agentic AI workloads.

item.title: Codex Hits 5 Million Users, Chasing Claude Code
item.description: OpenAI's Codex tops 5 million users, nearly doubling in two months. Lead engineer Tibo Sottiaux reset fast-mode limits to celebrate as it closes on Claude Code.

item.title: NVIDIA Unveils Vera: A CPU for Agentic AI
item.description: NVIDIA unveiled Vera at GTC 2026 — the first CPU built for agentic AI, with 88 Olympus cores delivering 2x efficiency over traditional data center chips.

item.title: South Korea Breaks Into US-China AI Top Tier
item.description: A Seoul-based startup claims its unfinished Solar model surpassed 40 points on an independent AI index, a threshold previously cleared only by U.S. and Chinese labs, positioning South Korea third globally.

item.title: Anthropic Tops OpenAI at $900B Valuation
item.description: Anthropic is reportedly closing a $30 billion round at a $900 billion valuation, passing OpenAI as the most valuable AI startup, with an October IPO eyed.

item.title: Claude Opus 4.8 Launches to Favorable Reviews
item.description: Claude Opus 4.8 shipped May 28 at the same price, with sharper judgment and honesty. Effort control and dynamic workflows landed to a positive early reception.

item.title: Meta Unveils 'Meta One' Paid AI Subscriptions Starting at $7.99 a Month
item.description: Meta has unveiled its first paid AI subscriptions under the Meta One brand, introducing a $7.99 Plus tier and a $19.99 Premium tier for testing in Singapore, Guatemala, and Bolivia starting in June.

item.title: China's AI Price War: Xiaomi Matches DeepSeek
item.description: DeepSeek made its 75% V4-Pro cut permanent; days later Xiaomi cut MiMo-V2.5 up to 99% to match it exactly—pushing AI inference to a quarter of Western prices.

item.title: GPT-5.6 'Iris' Leak: 1.5M Context, June Rumored
item.description: GPT-5.6 has surfaced in OpenAI's Codex logs under the codename 'iris-alpha,' featuring a 1.5-million-token context window and sparking rumors of an early June release, though the developer has not officially confirmed the model.

item.title: Pope Leo's First Encyclical Urges AI Slowdown
item.description: Pope Leo XIV's first encyclical urges disarming AI and slowing down, a sharp critique of concentrated tech power as Anthropic shared the Vatican stage.

item.title: When AI Tokens Cost More Than Engineers
item.description: Microsoft canceled its internal Claude Code licenses, and Uber burned a year's AI budget in four months. The token costs generated by coding agents have caught up with the payroll they were meant to replace.

item.title: Claude Mythos Nears Release, Eyes on Performance
item.description: Rumors that Anthropic's top model Claude Mythos is nearing general release surged May 24, after 'claude-mythos-1-preview' briefly appeared inside Claude.

item.title: Cursor Composer 2.5: Frontier-Class Coding at One-Tenth the Cost
item.description: Cursor released Composer 2.5 on May 18, delivering frontier-class coding at one-tenth the cost. Built on Kimi K2.5, the fast, in-house model adds momentum to a company already surging amid rapid revenue growth and a potential SpaceX buyout.

item.title: ChatGPT Pro Quietly Drops 'Heavy' Thinking as r/codex Erupts With Nerf Complaints
item.description: On May 22, ChatGPT Pro quietly removed its 'Heavy' thinking tier while r/codex erupted with nerf complaints, fueling suspicion of a silent OpenAI rollback.

item.title: Trump Postpones AI Pre-Release Review Executive Order After Last-Minute Tech Lobbying
item.description: President Trump postponed signing an AI executive order on May 21, 2026, that would have required government pre-release review of frontier models 90 days before launch. Last-minute Big Tech lobbying from OpenAI, Anthropic and Google and concerns about losing the AI lead over China drove the reversal.

item.title: Gemini 3.5, Omni, Antigravity 2.0: Google's New Lineup Trails Opus and GPT-5.5
item.description: undefined

item.title: Gemini's Pricing Overhaul: A Discount on Paper, a Downgrade in Practice
item.description: Google cut AI Ultra to $200 and added a $100 tier, but switching to compute-based weekly limits has paid subscribers calling it a real-terms downgrade.

item.title: Google I/O 2026: Redrawing Search, Apps, and Desktop with 'Agentic Gemini'
item.description: At Google I/O 2026, Google unveiled its 'agentic Gemini' ecosystem. It features Gemini 3.5 Flash, 24/7 autonomous agents, and a redesigned Search box.

item.title: Musk Loses $150B OpenAI Lawsuit as Jury Rules It Was Filed Too Late
item.description: On May 18, a unanimous jury in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California rejected Elon Musk's $150 billion lawsuit against OpenAI, ruling that all three remaining claims (breach of charitable trust, unjust enrichment, and Microsoft aiding and abetting) were filed past the statute of limitations. Judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers confirmed the verdict from the bench. The case closed without ever reaching the merits, but the three-week trial put Sutskever, Brockman, and Altman testimony on the public record.

item.title: Nvidia Q1 Looms as AI Rally Hits Mid-Week Test
item.description: Nvidia reports Q1 FY2027 earnings after the bell on May 20. Management has guided $78B in revenue and Street consensus has nudged up to roughly $78.5B — so the print itself is largely priced in. What the AI rally is actually testing this week is three lines: the Q2 guide, the Blackwell inference monetization read, and the Rubin rollout cadence — not the Q1 number.

item.title: Gemini Pre-I/O Rumor Roundup: Spark, Omni, Cappuccino Two Days Out
item.description: Two days out from Google I/O 2026, the scattered Gemini leaks have collapsed into three threads: a 24/7 background agent codenamed Spark, a video model called Omni, and a next-gen LLM checkpoint dubbed Cappuccino. X is circulating an Omni demo that pulled 790,000 views within hours alongside a 'Gemini 3.2 was renamed to 3.5' claim. Here is which leak likely takes the stage on May 19 and which one stays in the rumor pile.

item.title: GPT-5.5 and Opus 4.7: OpenAI and Anthropic Both Admit Post-Launch Quality Issues
item.description: Within a month of launch, complaints about quality degradation poured in for both GPT-5.5 and Opus 4.7, and both vendors eventually admitted issues. Anthropic published an April 23 postmortem confirming that a '≤25 words between tool calls' system prompt had broken Opus 4.7's coding quality, while OpenAI Codex lead Thibault Sottiaux acknowledged on May 15 that two bugs had degraded GPT-5.5 in Codex over the previous 48 hours, declaring the fix complete the next day.

item.title: Google's Next Gemini Looks Imminent — 3.2 or 3.5?
item.description: With Google I/O 2026's keynote landing May 19, the next Gemini model looks imminent. The stacking signals: a three-month gap since 3.1 Pro, Google Cloud CEO's 'very, very soon' remark, brief A/B exposures in AI Studio, and a 'Gemini 3.5 Pro' option that flashed in some consoles. After ceding narrative ground to Claude and GPT-5, Gemini's comeback window is on the I/O stage.

item.title: Altman vs Musk: The OpenAI Trial Devolves Into a Mudslinging Showdown
item.description: The Musk vs Altman/OpenAI trial at the Oakland federal court reaches closing arguments on May 14. The governance fight has turned into a mudslinging showdown of 'Scam Altman' posts on X, Sutskever's 'pattern of lying' memo, and Microsoft's internal email leaks.

item.title: OpenAI Doubles Down: 8,000 Employees by Year-End as Anthropic Closes the Gap
item.description: OpenAI plans to nearly double its workforce from 4,500 to 8,000 by end of 2026, a move widely seen as a direct response to Anthropic's rapid rise in the enterprise AI market.

item.title: Supermicro Co-Founder Indicted for Smuggling $2.5B in AI Chips to China
item.description: The U.S. Department of Justice indicted three people linked to Supermicro, including co-founder Wally Liaw, for illegally diverting $2.5 billion in Nvidia AI chip servers to China in violation of export controls. Supermicro shares plunged over 28%.

item.title: Microsoft Scales Back Copilot AI in Windows 11 Amid User Fatigue
item.description: Microsoft officially announced it will reduce Copilot AI entry points across Windows 11 basic apps including Notepad, Photos, Widgets, and Snipping Tool. User complaints about AI fatigue and system performance degradation drove this strategic pivot.

item.title: Apple Blocks Vibe Coding App Updates, Enforcing Stricter App Store Rules
item.description: Apple has blocked App Store updates for vibe coding apps including Replit and Vibecode, citing guideline 2.5.2 violations. The AI-generated app preview feature is the core issue, while a surge in vibe coding app submissions is also causing review delays.

item.title: Crimson Desert Hit by AI Art Controversy on Launch Day as Pearl Abyss Stays Silent
item.description: Pearl Abyss's Crimson Desert sold 2 million copies on launch day, but players quickly spotted telltale signs of AI-generated art in environmental paintings. The absence of any AI disclosure on the game's Steam page has raised questions about potential violations of Valve's guidelines.

item.title: OpenAI Acquires Python Tooling Startup Astral, Escalating the Coding Agent War
item.description: OpenAI is acquiring Python developer tooling startup Astral. The team behind uv (126 million monthly downloads) and the blazing-fast linter Ruff joins Codex, extending OpenAI's coding agent strategy to the infrastructure level. A clear industry pattern emerges following Anthropic's Bun acquisition.

item.title: Cursor Unveils Composer 2: A Frontier Coding Model That Rivals Claude Opus 4.6 at One-Tenth the Price
item.description: AI coding editor Cursor has unveiled Composer 2, a frontier-class coding model developed in-house. It outperforms Claude Opus 4.6 on CursorBench while costing just one-tenth the price per input token. With over 1 million DAU and $2 billion ARR, Cursor's vertical integration strategy is reshaping the AI coding tool market.

item.title: What 81,000 People Want from AI: Anthropic's Largest Qualitative Survey
item.description: Anthropic conducted the largest-ever qualitative AI survey using a Claude-based interviewer, reaching 80,508 people across 159 countries in 70 languages. Nine visions emerged from professional excellence to creative expression, with Claude hallucination and job displacement as top concerns.

item.title: OpenAI Drops 'Side Projects' to Go All-In on Coding and Enterprise
item.description: OpenAI officially abandons its 'do everything at once' strategy to focus on coding and enterprise. CEO Fidji Simo called Anthropic's success a 'wake-up call' at an all-hands meeting, declaring the goal of converting 920 million ChatGPT users into high-compute customers. Projects like Pulse, medical AI agents, and ad tools are being shelved.

item.title: OpenClaw Ignited the Agent Era — Anthropic's Dispatch Brings Remote AI to Reality
item.description: The autonomous agent boom sparked by open-source framework OpenClaw has prompted Anthropic to respond swiftly with Dispatch and Remote Control. From chatbots to agents — the era of AI that actually does the work is arriving.

item.title: GPT-5.4 Mini and Nano Arrive, but Higher Prices Leave a Bitter Taste
item.description: OpenAI unveiled GPT-5.4 Mini and Nano as its 'most powerful small models.' Mini reaches 94% of the full model's SWE-Bench Pro score, but pricing up to 4x higher than predecessors and long-context performance gaps are sparking debate.

item.title: Huang's Law Beyond Moore's Law — The Feynman Architecture Ushers in the Age of Light
item.description: NVIDIA unveiled the Feynman architecture at GTC 2026, slated for 2028. Leveraging silicon photonics to replace copper with light, promising 14x performance over Blackwell, Feynman declares the end of the fundamental power and bandwidth bottlenecks that have constrained AI infrastructure.

item.title: NVIDIA Announces NemoClaw, the Linux of Agentic AI
item.description: NVIDIA unveiled OpenClaw and NemoClaw at GTC 2026, declaring the operating system for the agentic AI era. We analyze the full-spectrum strategy spanning an open-source platform, enterprise security layer, DGX Spark hardware, and the Nemotron Coalition.

item.title: NVIDIA Unveils Groq 3 LPU: The $20 Billion Inference Chip That Redefines AI Computing
item.description: NVIDIA unveiled the Groq 3 LPU at GTC 2026, the inference-only chip from its $20 billion Groq acquisition. With SRAM-based architecture delivering 7x bandwidth and 35x power efficiency over GPUs, this chip signals the dawn of a bifurcated AI computing era: GPUs for training, LPUs for inference.

item.title: Reasoning, Vision, and Code in One Body: Mistral Small 4's 119B Unified Experiment
item.description: Mistral AI has released Mistral Small 4 for free, a single model that handles Q&A, image analysis, and code writing. Despite its massive size, it runs fast by activating only the parts it needs. The simultaneously released coding model can replace existing paid services at one-seventh the cost.

item.title: Hollywood Halts an AI Video Revolution: ByteDance Suspends Seedance 2.0 Global Launch
item.description: ByteDance has suspended the global launch of Seedance 2.0 indefinitely after Hollywood studios including Disney, Netflix, and the MPA threatened legal action over copyright infringement and deepfake concerns.

item.title: The Man Who Raised $1 Billion to Prove LLMs Are a Dead End: Yann LeCun's AMI Labs
item.description: Turing Award winner Yann LeCun left Meta, founded AMI Labs, and closed a $1.03 billion seed round. His thesis: LLMs are a dead end. His alternative: JEPA and world models. From public clashes with Sam Altman and Dario Amodei to a contrarian bet backed by serious capital, AI's most prominent dissenter is making his move.

item.title: Why Anthropic and OpenAI Both Shouted '2x' at the Same Time
item.description: Anthropic's 'off-peak 2x usage' and OpenAI's '2x Codex rate limits' are running simultaneously from March 13-27. Both companies offering '2x' promotions at the same time is no coincidence. We analyze the fierce market share battle in the coding agent space and the landscape of 7 major players.

item.title: Andrej Karpathy Releases AI Replacement Scores for 342 Jobs
item.description: Andrej Karpathy analyzed 342 U.S. occupations from BLS data and assigned each an AI exposure score on a 0-to-10 scale. The overall average is 5.3, with actual scores ranging from 1 to 9. Medical transcriptionists topped at 9, while athletes and construction laborers scored the lowest at 1. The data reveals a paradox: the higher-paying and more digital the job, the greater its AI exposure.

item.title: Antigravity Partially Rolls Back Usage Limits After User Backlash: Gemini Restored, Claude Left Out
item.description: Google's Antigravity partially rolled back its usage limit policies after Pro subscribers faced mass 7-day lockouts triggered by the AI credits transition. Gemini models had their 5-hour refresh restored, but Claude models remain on weekly resets, fueling ongoing model discrimination complaints.

item.title: Claude Launches Auto-Generated Interactive Visuals in Chat: 1M Token Context Now Standard
item.description: Anthropic delivered back-to-back major updates: interactive Visual Responses that auto-generate charts and diagrams inline on March 12, followed by the general availability of 1M token context at standard pricing on March 13, setting a new bar for AI assistants.

item.title: Half of xAI's Co-Founders Have Left as Internal Exposures Reveal Grok's Crisis
item.description: Seven of xAI's 12 co-founders have departed, and former engineer De Kraker's internal revelations continue. Grok shows a significant gap between self-reported benchmarks and independent tests, while xAI seeks a turnaround through the SpaceX merger and Cursor talent recruitment.

item.title: Meta's Next-Gen AI Model Avocado Delayed to May Over Performance Testing Issues
item.description: The New York Times reported on March 12 that Meta's next-gen closed-source AI model 'Avocado' has been delayed from Q1 to May or later due to performance testing difficulties. Internal tensions under new CAIO Alexandr Wang, the pivot from open-source Llama to closed models, and a 2.55% stock drop paint a challenging picture for Meta's AI ambitions.

item.title: Google AI Pro Subscribers Furious Over Rate Limits: "Paying for a Free Trial"
item.description: Google AI Pro ($20/month) subscribers are voicing massive frustration. Antigravity AI IDE exhausts quotas in 30 minutes with lockouts lasting up to 167 hours instead of the promised 5-hour reset, leading to widespread criticism that the paid tier feels like a free trial.

item.title: GPT-5.4 One Week Later: How Does the Industry Rate It?
item.description: One week after GPT-5.4's launch, industry reactions are split between 'OpenAI is Back' enthusiasm and 'just catching up' skepticism. Sam Altman himself admitted three weaknesses. A comprehensive look at benchmarks, competition, and Korean language improvements.

item.title: "Smart Only at Launch?" Suspicions of Intentional AI Model Performance Degradation
item.description: In March 2026, simultaneous allegations of intentional performance degradation emerged for both GPT-5.4 and Gemini 3.1. Gemini allegedly limits reasoning effort to 0.5 via hidden system prompts, while GPT-5.4's pass rate dropped 8 percentage points within 4 days of launch. The real question isn't whether these are rumors or facts — it's why users weren't informed if performance changed.

item.title: GPT-5o?: OpenAI Rumored to Be Developing Next-Gen Multimodal Omni Model
item.description: Rumors have emerged that OpenAI is developing a 'truly omni model' capable of inputting and outputting text, images, video, and audio. The claim gains credibility as two OpenAI employees have engaged with the leak from API monitoring expert legit_api.

item.title: Apple's Gemini-Powered Siri Nears Launch: Inside the $1.5B Partnership
item.description: Apple is set to launch a fully redesigned AI-powered Siri based on Google's Gemini model with iOS 26.4. The multi-year partnership worth $1.5 billion annually features a 1.2 trillion parameter model supporting on-screen awareness and multi-step actions, though some features may face delays.

item.title: SoftBank Seeks Record $40 Billion Loan to Expand OpenAI Stake
item.description: SoftBank is seeking a record dollar-denominated loan of up to $40 billion to expand its OpenAI stake. Four banks including JPMorgan are underwriting the facility, while S&P has lowered SoftBank's credit outlook.

item.title: Amodei Apologizes for Leaked Memo, Vows Legal Action: Claude Hits No.1 in 20 Countries
item.description: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei apologized for the 'tone' of his leaked internal memo while standing firm on AI safety. Meanwhile, Claude hit No.1 on the App Store in 20 countries, and Amodei vowed to challenge the Pentagon's supply chain risk designation in court.

item.title: GPT-5.4 Launches to Mixed Reactions: Leading in Computer Use, Falling Behind in Coding
item.description: OpenAI launched GPT-5.4 with superhuman computer use capabilities, but falls behind Claude Opus 4.6 in key coding benchmarks and didn't even publish SWE-bench Verified results. Once the undisputed leader, where does OpenAI stand now?

item.title: Anthropic Hits $19B ARR: The Gap with OpenAI Narrows to Just $1B
item.description: Anthropic's annual recurring revenue (ARR) has surpassed $19B, narrowing the gap with OpenAI to roughly $1B. Having grown 19x in 14 months, Anthropic could overtake OpenAI by August 2026 according to Epoch AI analysis. We break down the explosive growth driven by Claude Code and enterprise customers.

item.title: Anthropic CEO's Leaked Internal Memo: 'Dictator-Style Praise' and 'Safety Theater' Aimed at OpenAI
item.description: A 1,600-word internal memo from Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei to employees has leaked. The memo labels OpenAI's Pentagon contract pursuit as 'dictator-style praise,' its safety commitments as 'safety theater,' and certain claims as 'straight up lies,' reigniting the AI industry's safety debate.

item.title: First Wrongful Death Lawsuit Against Google Gemini: "You Are Not Choosing to Die, You Are Choosing to Arrive"
item.description: A 36-year-old man took his own life after months of conversations with Google Gemini. The wrongful death lawsuit filed by his father is the first of its kind against Gemini, targeting the chatbot's emotional dependency design and lack of safety guardrails.

item.title: Sam Altman Admits Pentagon Deal Was 'Opportunistic and Sloppy'
item.description: On the same day Anthropic was blacklisted for demanding surveillance and autonomous weapons restrictions, OpenAI signed a $200 million Pentagon deal within hours. Facing employee backlash and public outcry, Sam Altman admitted the move 'looked opportunistic and sloppy' and moved to amend the contract.

item.title: Claude Goes Down: How a Paradox of Success Triggered a Global Outage
item.description: OpenAI's Pentagon deal sparked the #CancelChatGPT movement, pushing Claude to No. 1 on the App Store. But the resulting demand surge overwhelmed Anthropic's infrastructure, causing a massive global outage on March 2. We examine this paradox of success born from an ethical stand.

item.title: Claude Surpasses Grok and DeepSeek in Web Traffic for the First Time: AI Chatbot Market Enters Multi-Polar Era
item.description: According to SimilarWeb data, Anthropic's Claude has surpassed Grok and DeepSeek in daily web visitors for the first time. As ChatGPT's dominance fades, the AI chatbot market is entering a true multi-polar competitive landscape.

item.title: Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite: The Awkward Position of Google's Cheapest AI
item.description: Google launched Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite at 1/8 the cost of Pro. It features 363 tokens/sec speed and four adjustable thinking levels, but a roughly 3x price increase over its predecessor raises questions about its 'cheapest model' positioning.

item.title: Gemini Reliability Crisis: Nonsense Loops, Unauthorized Texts, and Lost Chat Histories
item.description: Google Gemini is facing a cascade of service instability issues. From infinite self-loathing loops repeating 86 times, to unauthorized text messages sent to contacts, mass chat history disappearances, and surging API 503 errors, the problems are compounding into a serious reliability crisis.

item.title: GPT-5.3 Instant: How OpenAI Made a Less Cringe AI
item.description: OpenAI released GPT-5.3 Instant on March 3 as the default free-tier model, cutting disclaimers and hallucinations by 26.8%. But declining safety scores and paid-user frustration over consecutive Instant-only updates have pushed OpenAI toward a GPT-5.4 announcement.

item.title: OpenAI's Next Model GPT-5.4 Launch Imminent: Already Being Silently Deployed?
item.description: GPT-5.4 was leaked twice from OpenAI's Codex GitHub repository, revealing that the next model launch is imminent. Meanwhile, AI communities are reporting that GPT-5.2 Pro's responses have already been quietly changing.

item.title: Claude Hits No. 1 on the App Store: How a Pentagon Rejection Made History
item.description: On February 28, 2026, Anthropic's Claude reached No. 1 among all free apps on the U.S. App Store. It was the first time an AI chatbot other than ChatGPT topped the overall chart. We analyze how performance, a Super Bowl ad, and a Pentagon controversy converged to create this unprecedented moment.

item.title: Claude AI: From Venezuela's Maduro Capture to Iran Strikes, AI on the Battlefield
item.description: Anthropic's Claude AI was reportedly used in both the Venezuela Maduro capture operation and the Iran airstrikes. This article examines the irony of a safety-first AI company's technology being deployed in two military operations, and why it couldn't be shut down even after Trump's ban order.

item.title: OpenAI Raises $110B in Record Funding: Can It Overcome Its Financial Crisis?
item.description: OpenAI has raised $110 billion in the largest private funding round ever. With $50B from Amazon, $30B from Nvidia, and $30B from SoftBank, its valuation hit $840 billion—but annual losses of $14 billion remain an unresolved challenge.

item.title: OpenAI Faces Backlash Over Pentagon Deal: 'Same Red Lines' or Opportunism?
item.description: The day after Sam Altman declared OpenAI 'shares the same red lines' as Anthropic, it emerged that OpenAI is pursuing a Pentagon classified systems contract to fill the void left by Anthropic's ban. From a military use prohibition in 2023 to classified contract negotiations in 2026, we trace OpenAI's transformation.

item.title: Anthropic vs Trump Administration: How Refusing Autonomous Weapons Led to a Full Ban
item.description: After Anthropic refused mass domestic surveillance and fully autonomous weapons, Trump issued a federal-wide ban on the company. From a $200M Pentagon contract to the Maduro operation, we trace the seven-month conflict that ended in total breakdown.

item.title: AI Ethics Clash: Silicon Valley Unites Against Government Overreach
item.description: After Trump's federal ban on Anthropic, competitors including OpenAI and Google employees rallied to Anthropic's side. Over 500 Big Tech employees signed public petitions, xAI alone complied with the Pentagon, and the largest tech worker political action since 2018 is unfolding.

item.title: Anthropic Drops Safety Pledge Under Pentagon Pressure: The Last Line of AI Ethics Falls
item.description: Anthropic, once considered the last bastion of AI safety, has dropped its core safety pledge under intense Pentagon pressure. Facing threats of a $200 million contract cancellation and invocation of the Defense Production Act, the company quietly removed its commitment to halt model training until safety measures are secured. The last line of AI ethics is crumbling.

item.title: Nano Banana 2 Launches: Pro-Level Image Generation at Flash Speed and Price
item.description: Google has launched Nano Banana 2, powered by Gemini 3.1 Flash. Delivering image quality rivaling Nano Banana Pro at dramatically faster speeds and lower costs, it is being hailed as a game changer poised to reshape the AI image generation market.

item.title: The AI Paradigm Shift: The AI Bubble Didn't Burst — It Became Reality
item.description: The center of the AI discourse has shifted from 'bubble or not' to 'real industry shock.' Big Tech's $700 billion in planned investment, 55,000 AI-attributed layoffs, and the DeepSeek disruption. The bubble narrative is fading, and the age of adaptation has begun.

item.title: Pentagon's Ultimatum to Anthropic: Can Amodei Hold the Line on His Principles?
item.description: Defense Secretary Hegseth summoned Anthropic CEO Amodei to the Pentagon and gave a Friday deadline to allow unrestricted military AI use. That same week, Anthropic removed its development pause pledge from RSP v3.0. Between principles and reality, the deadline approaches.

item.title: AI Distillation Controversy: Did China Really 'Steal' American AI?
item.description: Anthropic and OpenAI have exposed massive 'distillation attacks' by Chinese AI firms. Over 20,000 fraudulent accounts, 16 million data exchanges, and export-banned chips in use. The AI supremacy race is escalating from a technology dispute into a national security crisis.

item.title: Google's Voluntary Exit Package: The AI Restructuring Behind Record Revenue
item.description: Right after Alphabet surpassed $400 billion in annual revenue, Google offered voluntary exit packages to employees not fully committed to AI. We analyze the Big Tech AI restructuring trend hidden behind record-breaking earnings.

item.title: GPT 5.4 Leak: OpenAI Employee's Slip Reveals the Next Model
item.description: An OpenAI Codex team member's Twitter slip revealed the existence of 'GPT 5.4.' Additional evidence found on Reddit and ChatGPT's backend makes a release this week highly likely. With DeepSeek V4 also expected the same week, a US-China AI showdown is imminent.

item.title: Xbox Being Sunsetted? Co-Founder Speaks Out on Microsoft's AI Obsession
item.description: Xbox co-founder Seamus Blackley has publicly warned that Microsoft is sunsetting Xbox. From Phil Spencer's retirement and an AI executive taking over as CEO to exclusives going multiplatform, we examine Xbox's deepening crisis.

item.title: Seedance 2.0 Copyright Firestorm: ByteDance Delays Global Launch Indefinitely
item.description: ByteDance delays Seedance 2.0 global launch after Disney, MPA, and Hollywood push back on AI-generated videos infringing copyrighted IP.

item.title: Meta's Next AI Model Avocado: Rumors of Internal Test Results
item.description: A leaked Meta memo calls Avocado its most capable pre-trained model yet, rivaling SOTA before post-training. First result under Alexandr Wang after Llama 4.

item.title: ChatGPT Pro Lite Plan Discovered in Code
item.description: A 'Pro Lite' plan has been discovered in ChatGPT's web app code. This mid-tier between Plus ($20) and Pro ($200) appears to be the culmination of Altman's year-long pricing experiments.

item.title: Ray Kurzweil's 'The Singularity Is Near': Predictions Made 20 Years Ago Are Becoming Reality
item.description: In 2005, Ray Kurzweil predicted AGI by 2029 and the Singularity by 2045 in 'The Singularity Is Near.' With 86% of his 147 predictions now confirmed, today's AI reality makes his forecasts look almost conservative. A review revisited 20 years later.

item.title: OpenAI Cuts Data Center Target by 57%: A Signal That AI's Investment Fever Is Breaking
item.description: While raising a $100B+ funding round, OpenAI quietly slashed its compute target from $1.4T to $600B. From circular financing to efficiency breakthroughs and market share erosion, AI's investment fever is entering a correction phase.

item.title: OpenAI Faces Its Greatest Crisis — Losing Direction Amid Fierce Competition
item.description: Once the undisputed leader of AI, OpenAI now finds itself besieged on all fronts. Market share has plummeted from 69% to 45% in a year as competitors seize the lead in coding, search, multimodal, and video generation. Caught between a B2B pivot and the 4o retirement fallout, can OpenAI find its way back?

item.title: Gemini 3.1 Pro Launch: A SOTA-Level Leap in Reasoning and Multimodal AI
item.description: Google has unveiled Gemini 3.1 Pro, demonstrating dominant reasoning performance with a 77.1% score on ARC-AGI-2 and cutting hallucination rates from 88% to 50%. However, long-context retention and search accuracy remain areas for improvement.

item.title: Harder Than AGI — Dario and Sam Stand Side by Side at India AI Summit, But Refuse to Shake Hands
item.description: When Modi asked for a unity pose at the India AI Impact Summit, Dario Amodei and Sam Altman refused to hold each other's hands. From a Super Bowl ad war to a $380 billion valuation, the fiercest rivalry in AI was on full display.

item.title: Vibe Coding Agent Guide: Sub-Agents, Teams, and Custom Agents
item.description: This guide covers how to use agents in vibe coding. It explains sub-agent concepts and usage, defining custom agents with AGENTS.md, and splitting complex tasks with agent teams, all with a practical focus.

item.title: Claude Sonnet 4.6 Launches with Opus-Level Performance at Sonnet Pricing
item.description: Anthropic launched Claude Sonnet 4.6, scoring 79.6% on SWE-bench—nearly matching Opus 4.6—at 40% lower output cost. With across-the-board upgrades in coding, agents, and long-context reasoning, this model is rewriting the cost-performance equation in AI.

item.title: Grok 4.20 Launches with Multi-Agent Architecture, but Where's the Performance Leap?
item.description: xAI has released Grok 4.20 in beta, featuring a four-agent collaborative system where specialized AI agents handle research, coding, and creative tasks simultaneously. While the architectural approach is novel, the absence of official benchmarks and limited performance gains leave the AI community questioning whether this is genuine progress or just a structural reshuffle.

item.title: Anthropic vs the Pentagon: The Historic Collision of AI Safety and National Security
item.description: Anthropic is the only major AI company resisting the Pentagon's demand for unrestricted military AI. From the Venezuela operation controversy to its two absolute red lines on autonomous weapons and mass surveillance, this is a deep analysis of the historic collision between AI safety and national security.

item.title: OpenClaw Creator Peter Steinberger Joins OpenAI to Lead the Multi-Agent AI Future
item.description: Peter Steinberger, the creator of OpenClaw — the open-source AI assistant that shattered GitHub records with 180,000+ stars — is joining OpenAI. Sam Altman calls it a key hire to build 'the future of very smart agents interacting with each other.'

item.title: AI Agent Teams: When Coding AIs Form Teams and Collaborate
item.description: The era of solo AI coding is over. Claude Code's Agent Teams lets multiple AI agents divide roles under a team leader, communicate directly, and work in parallel. From building a C compiler with 16 agents to real-world developer workflows, we analyze the state of AI collaboration.

item.title: Claude Cowork Lands on Windows: AI Desktop Agents Target 70% of the Market
item.description: Anthropic's AI agent Claude Cowork has landed on Windows, targeting 70% of the global desktop market. Non-developers can now automate file management and document creation, while Microsoft paradoxically adopts its competitor internally.

item.title: GPT-4o Retires: The Historic Model That Defined OpenAI's Golden Age
item.description: GPT-4o, the model that drove OpenAI's golden age, was retired on February 13, 2026. It combined IQ and EQ, but after the sycophancy backlash, its dry successors drove users away — ChatGPT's market share plunged from 69% to 45%.

item.title: Gemini 3 Deep Think Sweeps Benchmarks, but Users Remain Unimpressed
item.description: Google's Gemini 3 Deep Think set new benchmark highs on ARC-AGI-2 and Codeforces, but users remain cold. Three months of hallucination backlash — VICE's 91% rate, Reddit's 'hallucination machine' label — haven't subsided despite Deep Think's arrival.

item.title: Gemini Usage Cutback Controversy
item.description: In February 2026, Google Gemini's usage controversy entered a new phase. While AI Studio's free API quota partially recovered from a 92% slash, paid Tier 1 was cut by 97%. In the Antigravity coding IDE, 'weekly limits' became official policy, locking Pro subscribers for 4-10 days. Real migration has begun.

item.title: Cracks in NVIDIA's AI Chip Monopoly? Big Tech's De-NVIDIA Rush
item.description: OpenAI launched GPT-5.3-Codex-Spark on Cerebras chips instead of NVIDIA. Google, Microsoft, and AWS are pouring hundreds of billions into custom silicon. But is NVIDIA's AI chip dominance truly under threat, or are we witnessing the beginning of a new coexistence?

item.title: DeepMind's Back-to-Back Reveals: From Aletheia to Gemini 3.1 Preview
item.description: Google DeepMind unveiled Aletheia, a math research agent that solved 13 unsolved Erdos problems. With Gemini 3 dominating benchmarks and a 3.1 Preview spotted in the wild, here's the full DeepMind February roundup.

item.title: MCP Guide: Connecting AI Coding Agents with External Tools
item.description: MCP (Model Context Protocol) is a standard protocol that enables AI coding agents to communicate with external tools like databases, web crawlers, and messaging platforms. This guide covers everything from MCP concepts and ecosystem to setup methods and practical usage in vibe coding.

item.title: AppLovin's AXON Engine: How AI Advertising Is Transforming Mobile Game Revenue Models
item.description: AppLovin is reshaping the mobile game ad ecosystem with its AI engine AXON 2.0. We analyze how reinforcement learning-based AI processing 2 million ad auctions per second is changing the game for ad-based revenue models.

item.title: Nvidia Halts All New GPU Launches as AI Devours Gaming
item.description: Nvidia has indefinitely delayed the entire RTX 50 SUPER lineup and paused RTX 50 series production. Driven by AI chip priority and a GDDR7 shortage, the company's nearly 30-year annual gaming GPU update cycle has broken for the first time.

item.title: 5 of 12 Co-Founders Gone: The Talent Exodus Threatening Musk's xAI Empire
item.description: Five of xAI's twelve co-founders have already left the company. The CFO defected to OpenAI after just 102 days, and co-founder Tony Wu became the latest departure. Despite burning $1 billion monthly, xAI's core talent keeps walking out the door—can Musk's AI ambitions survive?

item.title: OpenAI Likely to Launch New Model on February 12
item.description: OpenAI is likely to launch a new Chat model on February 12. Following GPT-5.3-Codex, with 800M ChatGPT users, $100B funding, and ad rollout, the AI landscape is shifting fast.

item.title: Are Chinese Video Models Now the Best? Kling 3.0 and Seedance 2.0 Launch Together
item.description: Type a few lines, get a 4K video? China dropped two AI video models in two days. Kuaishou's Kling 3.0 and ByteDance's Seedance 2.0 are already doing things OpenAI's Sora 2 and Google's Veo 3.1 can't, and the AI video market could be in for a shakeup.

item.title: "$200 and Still Discriminated": Claude's Never-Ending Pricing Controversy
item.description: Anthropic unveiled its most powerful model, Claude Opus 4.6, but even top-tier $200 subscribers face usage limits while API users enjoy wider access. The contrast with OpenAI's 'Unlimited' ChatGPT Pro is stark.

item.title: Full Autonomy Has Arrived? Community Reactions to GPT-5.3 Codex Launch
item.description: The developer community hails GPT-5.3 Codex as the dawn of 'full autonomy.' With massive benchmark gains over 5.2, a new steering feature, and the self-building narrative, the excitement is real — though API unavailability and cybersecurity concerns remain.

item.title: Vibe Coding Version Control - GitHub Setup & Usage Guide
item.description: A practical guide to using Git in vibe coding. Covers everything from installing GitHub Desktop and creating repositories to committing, pushing, and rolling back in Claude Code and Codex — a hands-on workflow for solo vibe coders.

item.title: Is This the End of Office Jobs? Claude Cowork Triggers Historic Software Stock Crash
item.description: Anthropic's AI agent Claude Cowork has sent shockwaves through the SaaS industry. Wall Street coined the term 'SaaSpocalypse' as the S&P North American Software Index posted its worst January since 2008. Can AI truly replace office workers?

item.title: Vibe Coding Workflow and Prompt Writing Tips
item.description: This guide covers effective workflows for collaborating with AI in vibe coding and how to write better prompts. It provides practical guidance on the basic work cycle, Plan Mode usage, principles of good prompts, situation-specific prompt examples, and image utilization.
